Source src/experiments/star-field/engine/bodies/primitives.ts
UX surface Boot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

SF_USER_BODY

userData key carrying the body id from mesh → raycast hit.

SF_USER_PROXY

userData flag marking an invisible oversized pick proxy — picking prefers a real-mesh hit down the ray so proxy bubbles never eclipse the bodies they overlap.

makePickProxy

Invisible pick bubble for bodies too small to hit reliably — planets and moons under SF_DETAIL.PICK_MIN world units subtend a handful of pixels at the home camera, so a slightly larger transparent sphere (riding inside mesh to inherit orbit position and spin) gives the raycaster a usable target. Marked SF_USER_PROXY so a real-mesh hit along the same ray always wins; the caller stamps the body id on userData since the proxy is shared across kinds.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param radius The body's true radius — the proxy scales with it so
  • @returns The invisible proxy mesh.

makeGlowSphereMaterial

Luminous-sphere node material — a star's disc must not read as a flat polygon. The fresnel rim (1 − |view·n|)^falloff mixes the body's color/texture toward the limb tint and dips the alpha at the extreme silhouette, so the photosphere dissolves into its additive halo instead of cutting a hard circle against the sky. Built as a MeshBasicNodeMaterial — the WebGPURenderer node pipeline rejects classic GLSL ShaderMaterials.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param deps TSL namespace + node-material ctors (bootstrap-injected).
  • @param colorHex Core tint (def.color; SUN_LIGHT fallback).
  • @param tex Optional photosphere texture — modulates the core.
  • @param rimTint Limb color (hot rim for stars, muted for moons).
  • @param falloff Fresnel exponent — higher keeps a tight bright core.

irregularGeometry

Triaxial rubble-pile geometry for def.irregular bodies — a detail-4 icosahedron crumpled by seeded value noise so the silhouette dimples like a captured asteroid instead of reading as a hydrostatic ball. Every vertex sits on the sphere (r = def.radius); the displacement d = 1 + vnoise(unit·octaves)·amp pushes it along its own normal, then axes stretches the solid into the body's true triaxial proportions (Phobos ≈ 27×22×18 km → [1, 0.81, 0.67]). Per-vertex spherical UVs (u = atan2 longitude, v = asin latitude) are baked from the PRE-stretch unit direction so an equirect map still wraps pole-to-pole without smearing across the crumpled facets.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param def Catalog entry — irregular carries amp + optional axes.
  • @returns Crumpled geometry with spherical UVs + smooth normals.

makeSphere

Sphere + material for a solid body — textured when the catalog maps one, tinted procedural otherwise. Stars/systems use the fresnel-limb node material (they emit their own light); planets and smaller get lit MeshStandard. When sunDir is passed (day/night registry vector) the body upgrades to MeshStandardNodeMaterial so the emissive layer can be gated by the sun direction — city lights never glow on the lit hemisphere.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param deps TSL namespace + node-material ctors.
  • @param def Catalog entry.
  • @param texMap Loaded texture map keyed by URL.
  • @param sunDir Shared sun-direction vector (mutated per frame by

makeCloudShell

Extra translucent sphere one shell above a surface — Earth's cloud deck rides a white-on-black map under additive blending so the dark sky between clouds contributes nothing; the deck scales slightly past the surface sphere so it reads as atmosphere, not paint.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param def Catalog entry (radius sizes the shell).
  • @param cloudTex The loaded cloud map (caller guards its presence).

makeAtmoShell

Atmosphere rim shell — a fresnel-limb translucent sphere just past the surface whose tint migrates with the sun direction: deep blue on the night limb, bright scattering blue on the day limb, and a warm amber band through the terminator (rayleigh→mie analogy). Opacity also dims on the night side so the rim reads thinnest where the air is unlit. updateDayNight keeps the shared sunDir vector current.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param deps TSL namespace + node-material ctors (bootstrap-injected).
  • @param def Catalog entry — def.atmosphere scales the base opacity.
  • @param sunDir Shared sun-direction vector (mutated per frame).

makeStarHalo

Additive halo sprite behind a luminous body — stars and the Sun glow like point sources on a real long-exposure frame instead of rendering as flat colored balls. Kept off the LOD detail list: a star's glow IS its far-field representation.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param def Catalog entry (color tints the halo).
  • @param glowTex Shared radial-gradient glow texture (may be undefined).
  • @param flat Point-star mode — a filled core glow (no photosphere behind

makeShell

Translucent shell layer — Venus's haze atmosphere and Saturn's ring get a secondary texture-mapped surface parented to the main mesh. Returns the created Object3D so the caller can register it as LOD detail.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param def Catalog entry.
  • @param shellTexture Shell texture URL — narrowed non-null by the caller's
  • @param parent The primary mesh the shell rides on.
  • @param texMap Loaded texture map keyed by URL.

posAttr

RingGeometry ships planar UVs (the ring occupies uv-space like a circle inscribed in a square), but the Saturn strip texture is radius-indexed — u sweeps inner→outer across the banded ring face. Remap each vertex's u to its normalized radius (v rides the strip's center row) so the C/B/A ring bands and the Cassini gap land at their true radii instead of smearing into a solid plate.

makeStation

Crafted-station silhouette — a crewed orbiter (the ISS) is not a ball of light: a long truss carries a pressurized-module core at centre and a pair of wide flat solar-array wings at the tips, all in lit MeshStandardMaterial so the station glints in sunlight and goes dark through eclipse instead of glowing. All proportions derive from sat.radius so the model shrinks with the solar tier.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param sat Satellite def — radius is the core scale unit.
  • @returns The station group (caller positions it on its pivot).

makeSatellites

Decorative companion satellites — small unlit spheres on child pivots; sat.station swaps the glow ball for the crafted truss-and-panels model (ISS). satPivots returns the {pivot,speed,phase} records frame.ts rotates.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param deps TSL namespace + node-material ctors.
  • @param def Catalog entry — satellites lists the companions.
  • @param mesh The host body mesh — pivots attach to it to orbit.
